explanations: terra: The buyer of magic has مَا لَهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلَاقٍ; the source's dictionary form “share” becomes the loss incurred by a chosen exchange.
terra: Righteousness includes giving wealth despite loving it and joins that act to belief and reverence; this closely matches 92's sequence of giving, taqwa, and affirming the best.
terra: God intends ease and does not intend hardship in the fasting ruling; this is the ordinary y-s-r sense that the source sets beside the root's secondary gambling sense.

luna: The section identifies خَلَاق from the خ ل ق root as a share. This verse uses خَلَاق to deny an afterlife share to those who ask only for worldly life, making the portion depend on what they seek. | terra: وَمَا لَهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلَاقٍ uses خَلَاق in the source's dictionary sense of an allotted share: asking only for the nearer world leaves no share in the last.

terra: Between the person with no afterlife share in 2:200 and the earned share in 2:202, this petitioner asks the Lord for good in both the world and the hereafter, preserving both realms rather than choosing only the nearer one.

luna: After people ask for good in both lives, this verse says each has a share of what they earned. It connects the section's dictionary sense of share to outcomes grounded in conduct rather than a draw. | terra: أُولَئِكَ لَهُمْ نَصِيبٌ مِّمَّا كَسَبُوا gives the two-world petitioners a share from what they earned; نَصِيب is the source's dictionary gloss for خَلَاق and replaces lucky allotment with accountable acquisition, answering 2:200.

luna: The section's maysir scene meets this verse's paired questions about gambling and what to spend: it puts taking a chance for a share beside giving from one's means. | terra: This ayah itself places الْمَيْسِرِ, the y-s-r family's gambling sense developed in the source, beside the question of what to spend; قُلِ الْعَفْوَ turns an accidental gaming share into a deliberate surplus given away.
terra: The good loan to God is multiplied many times, while God constricts and expands and to Him people return; the apparent borrower is the one who controls every allotment.

terra: Israel objects to Saul's kingship because he lacks abundant wealth, but the prophet says God chose him and gives His dominion to whom He wills; divine selection overturns wealth-based entitlement.
terra: The Throne Verse says that whatever is in the heavens and earth belongs to God and ends by naming Him the Most High; possession and height are attributes of the owner.
luna: The verse pictures spending in God's way as seed yielding multiplied grain. It gives a concrete return from giving, in contrast to seeking material gain through the section's chance-based game.
terra: Those who spend and do not follow the gift with reminder or injury receive their reward with their Lord; the giver relinquishes both property and a claim over the recipient.

luna: The verse warns that charity is undone by reminders of one's favor or by injury. That sets a boundary around the section's giver who is owed no recompense and acts without a debt to collect. | terra: Charity nullified by reminder, injury, or display reverses 92:19–20's gift free of human leverage and directed only to the Lord's face.
terra: Spending ابْتِغَاءَ مَرْضَاتِ اللَّهِ makes divine pleasure the giver's aim and turns the amount given into fruit rather than a gaming return.

luna: This verse says that spending is for the giver, must be done seeking God's face, and will be repaid in full by God. It makes the section's claim that no human favor is being repaid especially concrete: the giver seeks God, not a debtor's return. | terra: وَمَا تُنفِقُونَ إِلَّا ابْتِغَاءَ وَجْهِ اللَّهِ is the closest formulation of the giver's sole purpose in 92:20 and locates repayment of the gift with God.
terra: لَن تُغْنِيَ عَنْهُمْ أَمْوَالُهُمْ ... مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئًا repeats the limit on wealth's power and places its owners at the fire, though it lacks the source's falling image.

terra: Heaped gold and silver and other desired possessions are described as worldly enjoyment, while the best return is with God; visible property is set against what is held at the true destination.

luna: The verse says dominion is given or taken by God, who honors and humbles whom He wills. It locates rank and possession in God's hand, unlike the section's arrow game where a high-value draw wins a share. | terra: مَالِكَ الْمُلْكِ gives dominion and removes it, exalts and abases; the true owner actively allots rank and property rather than surrendering them to chance.

luna: The verse stages a drawing of lots (يُلْقُونَ أَقْلَامَهُمْ) to decide who will care for Mary. This parallels the section's lot-drawn assignment, while the outcome is a duty of care rather than a material stake. | terra: The guardians cast their pens to decide who would care for Mary; this is a noncommercial lot for responsibility, a concrete counter-scene to arrows drawn for shares of meat.

luna: The section's dictionary form الخَلَاق, from root خ ل ق, means a share. This verse says those who sell their covenant for a small price have no share in the Hereafter, and adds that God will not purify them. | terra: لَا خَلَاقَ لَهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ makes the sold covenant yield no final share, and وَلَا يُزَكِّيهِمْ reverses the giver's self-purification in 92:18.

luna: The verse says righteousness is not reached until one spends from what one loves. It makes the section's act of giving wealth a specific test of what is valued. | terra: لَن تَنَالُوا الْبِرَّ حَتَّى تُنفِقُوا مِمَّا تُحِبُّونَ makes surrender of valued property the path to goodness and says God knows every expenditure.

luna: The verse says disbelievers' wealth and children will not avail them against God and names the Fire as their end. It repeats the section's limit on مال as protection in the Hereafter. | terra: The same formula says the disbelievers' wealth and children will not avail against God at all; it is a repeated Quranic boundary on apparent possession.
luna: The verse describes the God-conscious as spending in both prosperity and adversity. It makes the section's giving a chosen stance across circumstances, not an ease that depends on chance.
terra: Whoever desires the world's reward is given from it, and whoever desires the hereafter's reward is given from it; God, rather than the desirer, dispenses each return.

luna: After condemning stinginess, the verse says the inheritance of the heavens and earth belongs to God. It supports the section's claim that the holder of wealth is not its final owner. | terra: The ayah condemns withholding what God gave and ends وَلِلَّهِ مِيرَاثُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ; hoarded wealth finally returns to its actual owner.

luna: The section's dictionary form الخَلَاق means a portion or share; here inheritance is assigned to men and women as a prescribed share (نَصِيبًا مَفْرُوضًا), a fixed entitlement rather than a chance division. | terra: Men and women each have نَصِيبٌ مَّفْرُوضٌ from inherited property; this is a legally fixed share, sharply distinct from the camel portion won by an arrow.
terra: When relatives, orphans, and the poor attend the division, the heirs are told to provide for them from it; this places voluntary giving at the edge of a formally allotted estate.

luna: This verse sets distinct inheritance portions for children and parents. It gives a concrete example of measured property shares assigned by rule, unlike the section's chance-drawn division. | terra: God Himself assigns male and female inheritance portions and calls them فَرِيضَةً مِّنَ اللَّهِ; the created pair of 92:3 thus receives measured property shares from the owner.

luna: The verse assigns fixed inheritance portions to spouses and certain siblings. It continues the measured divisions in 4:11 and shows the section's idea of apportioned shares applied to property by rule. | terra: The spouse and sibling shares continue God's detailed apportionment in 4:11, showing property cut into known obligations rather than lucky portions.

luna: The verse says not to covet what God has given some over others and that each has a share of what they earn (نَصِيبٌ مِمَّا اكْتَسَبُوا). It gives an earned portion as a counterpart to the section's share won by lot. | terra: Do not covet what God gave some over others; men and women each have a share of what they earned and are told to ask God, locating both earning and bounty outside envious chance.
terra: God appoints heirs for what parents and relatives leave and commands that covenant partners be given their share; property succession and a due portion are assigned rather than gambled for.
terra: Those who are stingy, urge stinginess, and hide what God gave from His bounty treat allotted provision as private mastery rather than a trust to be shared.

luna: The verse criticizes people who claim purity for themselves and says God purifies whom He wills. It places a boundary around the section's giver who gives to purify himself: purification is not a self-awarded possession.
terra: أَمْ لَهُمْ نَصِيبٌ مِّنَ الْمُلْكِ joins “share” and “dominion” exactly; their refusal to give people even a speck shows why possessing a portion does not make one its generous lord.
terra: A person who intercedes for good or evil has a نَصِيب or كِفْل from it; the source's “share” becomes a moral consequence generated by participation rather than chance.

terra: Final outcome is not بِأَمَانِيِّكُمْ nor the wishes of another community but follows deeds; this supplies the accountability boundary behind 53:24's denial that a person owns whatever he wishes.
terra: The believer who does righteous acts, male or female, enters the Garden without even a speck of injustice; this continues 4:123 by joining the created pair to an accurately earned outcome.
terra: Whoever wants worldly reward is reminded that with God are the rewards of both world and hereafter; both possible portions remain at one source.

terra: The concluding inheritance ruling measures sibling shares, including the male's portion relative to two females, and closes that God clarifies so people do not stray; allocation and guidance thus meet.

luna: The section describes shares drawn by arrows from a slaughtered camel; this verse forbids seeking a portion by divining arrows (الأزلام) and also names carrion. It marks the boundary around that lottery scene. | terra: وَأَن تَسْتَقْسِمُوا بِالْأَزْلَامِ directly names seeking a share by arrows, while الْمُتَرَدِّيَةُ in the same ayah recalls the source's تَرَدَّى scene; both the lot and the fallen carcass are placed under divine prohibition rather than chance ownership.

luna: The section's maysir is listed with divining arrows (الأزلام) among forbidden practices. Its wording to avoid them, فاجتنبوه, shares the ج ن ب root the section notes in 92:17, where the God-fearing are kept away from the Fire. | terra: الْمَيْسِرُ and الْأَزْلَامُ name both the game and its arrows, and فَاجْتَنِبُوهُ uses the j-n-b family echoed by the God-fearing giver being kept away from the fire in 92:17.

luna: This continues the prohibition in 5:90 and names gambling's own consequence: Satan seeks hostility and distraction from prayer through it. That gives the section's chance-based pursuit of shares a social and devotional cost. | terra: This continuation of 5:90 names الْخَمْرِ وَالْمَيْسِرِ again and shows the game's actual distribution—enmity, hatred, and diversion from remembrance and prayer—rather than beneficial provision.
terra: Worldly life is called play and amusement, while the hereafter is better for the reverent; it places the source's game inside a wider contrast between temporary play and final value.

luna: The verse says its speakers assign a portion of crops and livestock to God and another to their partners. This is a direct livestock-allocation scene, but the section's account locates true ownership with the Lord rather than humanly assigned shares. | terra: The idolaters manufacture one share for God and one for their partners from crops and cattle; the ayah condemns creatures acting as owners who allot God's provision by claim.

luna: Continuing the arbitrary livestock portions in 6:136, this verse describes crops and animals declared inaccessible to all but those the speakers choose, and animals restricted by their claims. Its own detail is who may take from the allotment.

luna: The same allocation passage specifies that what is in some animals' wombs is reserved for males and forbidden to wives, while a dead birth is shared. It supplies a particularly concrete, gendered division of livestock portions.

luna: This completes the livestock passage by condemning the killing of children and prohibiting what God provided. It identifies the cost of fabricated rules over provision, beyond the preceding verses' partition scheme.
terra: God produces cultivated goods and commands that their due be given on harvest day; the owner receives produce yet must release its share under the Producer's command.

luna: The section explains the word رَبّ as owner and quotes the dictionary form “Lord of everything.” This verse states of God, وَهُوَ رَبُّ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ, anchoring the section's claim that the allotter and owner is the Lord. | terra: أَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ أَبْغِي رَبًّا وَهُوَ رَبُّ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ voices the source dictionary's “Lord of every thing,” then makes each soul answer for what it earns.
terra: God makes people successors on earth, raises some in degrees, and tests them through what He gave; delegated possession and unequal portions are explicitly a trial.
terra: يَنَالُهُمْ نَصِيبُهُم مِّنَ الْكِتَابِ portrays a decreed portion reaching wrongdoers before death; it is a less material instance of an allotted share arriving from a prior measure.
terra: Wealth and children are a trial, while the great reward is with God; apparent possessions test their holder rather than certify his allotted worth.

luna: This verse assigns a fifth of war gains to named recipients, including the needy and orphans. It is another material-share scene where the portion is prescribed, not won by arrows. | terra: The spoils ayah fixes named fractions and recipients and first says أَنَّ لِلَّهِ خُمُسَهُ; gained property is divided under divine title rather than by a lucky arrow.

luna: The verse condemns those who hoard gold and silver rather than spend it in God's way. It gives the section's withholding of مال a concrete form with a stated consequence. | terra: Those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in God's way turn accumulated property into the cause of painful punishment rather than security.

luna: This continues the hoarding warning of 9:34: the hoarded metal becomes a punishment, and the verse identifies it as what they stored for themselves. It shows stored wealth turning against its holder. | terra: The hoarded metal of 9:34 is heated and used to brand its owners, who are told to taste what they stored; the kept share becomes the instrument of recompense.
terra: God makes His word the highest; this provides a Quranic “highest” whose value comes from divine truth rather than being the most valuable arrow in a case.
terra: The Prophet is told not to admire their wealth and children because God may punish them through those very possessions in worldly life; a large share can be an instrument of loss.

terra: فَاسْتَمْتَعُوا بِخَلَاقِهِمْ uses خَلَاق for the worldly portion earlier peoples consumed; the ayah then likens later people to them, showing an allotted share spent away rather than retained for the last.
terra: Some covenant that if God gives from His bounty they will give charity; the promised gift is explicitly conditional on first receiving an allotment from God.
terra: When God gives them from His bounty, they withhold and turn away; this continuation makes received provision reveal the same miserly path as 92:8 and 92:16.
terra: This repeated warning again says not to admire wealth and children, through which their owners may be punished before dying unbelieving; possession reverses into burden.
terra: خُذْ مِنْ أَمْوَالِهِمْ صَدَقَةً تُطَهِّرُهُمْ وَتُزَكِّيهِم ties wealth given away to purification, making explicit the relation compressed in 92:18.
terra: God has purchased believers' lives and wealth in exchange for the Garden; human possession is nested inside a divine transaction whose final payment is the hereafter.
terra: Those who desire worldly life and its adornment are paid their deeds there in full; a nearer portion can be completely allotted while still excluding the last.
terra: The people described in 11:15 have nothing in the hereafter but fire, so full worldly payment proves no final share.
terra: وَإِنَّا لَمُوَفُّوهُمْ نَصِيبَهُمْ غَيْرَ مَنقُوصٍ promises the idolaters their undiminished portion, making the final allotment exact even when it is punishment.
terra: God expands and restricts provision, while people rejoice in worldly life though it is only slight enjoyment beside the hereafter; size of present allotment and final value are separated.
terra: Divine treasuries hold every thing and it descends only بِقَدَرٍ مَّعْلُومٍ; the human portion is a measured release from what remains with its owner.
terra: They assign لِمَا لَا يَعْلَمُونَ نَصِيبًا مِّمَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ; the false religious share is carved from provision whose giver is God.
terra: The highest attribute belongs to God, while the evil description belongs to those who deny the hereafter; “highest” is removed from material rank and attached to its owner.

luna: The verse says God has favored some over others in provision, then asks whether recipients would share it equally with those under their authority. It describes unequal shares as provision from God, not winnings from an arrow draw. | terra: God favors some over others in provision, yet the favored resist making those they possess equal partners in it; the ayah exposes selective human claims while asking whether God's favor is denied.

terra: Do not exchange God's covenant for a small price, because what is with God is better; immediately before 16:96's contrast between perishing human holdings and what remains with God, this identifies one way a final share is sold away.

luna: The section's gloss for عِندَهُ describes what is present or near, and it asks who owns what a person has. This verse contrasts what is with people and ends with what is with God, which remains (مَا عِنْدَكُمْ يَنْفَدُ وَمَا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ بَاقٍ). | terra: مَا عِندَكُمْ يَنفَدُ وَمَا عِندَ اللَّهِ بَاقٍ uses “with/at” as possession and sets perishing human holdings against what remains with God.

terra: The ayah binds each person's “bird” to his neck and brings out his record at resurrection; if ṭāʾir is heard as fortune, it relocates fate from an external omen or lot to the person's disclosed account.
terra: The one who wants the immediate world receives only what God wills and for whom He wills; desire does not itself determine the worldly allotment.
terra: The one who desires the hereafter, believes, and strives for it has that striving appreciated; continuing 17:18, the final portion follows directed effort rather than a fortunate draw.
terra: كُلًّا نُّمِدُّ ... مِنْ عَطَاءِ رَبِّكَ says both groups are extended from the Lord's gift, identifying the common provider behind their different aims in 17:18–19.
terra: Worldly gradations are surpassed by the hereafter's greater degrees; this completes 17:18–20 by distinguishing a present allotment from the higher final one.
terra: Give the relative, poor person, and traveler their due and do not squander; property held by one person already contains apportioned claims of others.
terra: The command neither to keep one's hand chained nor extend it completely sets a measured boundary for giving instead of leaving distribution to impulse.
terra: The Lord expands and restricts provision for whom He wills; following the spending boundary in 17:29, this identifies who measures the giver's own resources.
luna: This verse commands full measure and just weighing in trade. It offers an economic counterpart to the section's measured shares: a just quantity rather than a portion fixed by a lottery.
terra: If people possessed the treasuries of the Lord's mercy, they would withhold for fear of spending; the hypothetical makes miserliness the decisive difference between human and divine ownership.
terra: The garden owner boasts that he has more wealth and a stronger company; his possessive comparison begins a scene that tests whether abundance makes him master.
terra: His companion answers the boast by invoking the one who created him from dust and a drop and fashioned him as a man; creaturely origin corrects the owner's claim.

terra: The owner should have entered his garden saying that it is what God willed and that power belongs only to God, even while seeing his companion as poorer in wealth; possession requires acknowledgment of its source.
terra: The garden's fruit is destroyed and its owner regrets what he spent on it and associating partners with his Lord; “his” property vanishes under the Lord's prior claim.
terra: No group can help the garden owner apart from God, and he cannot save himself; this distinguishes social possession from the power that actually preserves it.
terra: At that point authority belongs to God, the Real, who is best in reward and outcome; the ruined-property scene resolves in true ownership and final recompense.

luna: The verse calls wealth and children adornments of worldly life, while enduring good deeds are better. It adds what lasts to the section's claim that possession cannot secure the Hereafter. | terra: Wealth and children are the adornment of nearer life, while lasting good deeds are better عِندَ رَبِّكَ; the verse contrasts held property with what remains at the Lord.
terra: The believer who acts rightly receives the best reward and an easy command; moral action, recompense, and yusr meet without any gaming allotment.

luna: After sacrificial camels are slaughtered, this verse directs people to eat from them and feed the needy. It recalls the section's divided camel, while locating its distribution in worship and care rather than a lottery. | terra: The sacrificial camels are made God's rites, then their meat is eaten and shared with the contented and the asker; this is the source's slaughtered-camel distribution transformed from gambling into worship and provision.

luna: This explains the camel offering in 22:36: neither its meat nor blood reaches God; piety does. It separates the material shares in the section's scene from the devotion that gives an offering its value. | terra: Neither the camel's meat nor blood reaches God, but piety does; continuing 22:36, it makes the moral intention—not the size of a drawn portion—the value of the division.
terra: Do they think the wealth and sons supplied to them prove something about their standing? The question isolates the mistaken inference from a large worldly allotment.
terra: نُسَارِعُ لَهُمْ فِي الْخَيْرَاتِ rejects the inference posed in 23:55; abundant provision is not necessarily the final good its holder imagines.
terra: وَآتُوهُم مِّن مَّالِ اللَّهِ الَّذِي آتَاكُمْ calls the property being transferred “God's wealth” even while it is in human hands, exactly clarifying delegated ownership.

luna: The section's root خ ل ق carries the dictionary sense of a measured portion. This verse says God created everything and measured it precisely (فَقَدَّرَهُ تَقْدِيرًا), a direct formulation of creation under measure. | terra: The one to whom the dominion belongs خَلَقَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ فَقَدَّرَهُ تَقْدِيرًا; ownership, creation, and exact apportionment meet in the same sentence, as the source's خَلَقَ wordplay proposes.
terra: Abraham identifies his Lord as the one who created him and therefore guides him; creation and guidance are one Lord's acts, as 92:3, 92:12, and 92:20 imply.

luna: The verse says that on the Day wealth and children will not avail anyone. This is a direct afterlife counterpart to the section's claim that a man's مال cannot help him when he falls. | terra: يَوْمَ لَا يَنفَعُ مَالٌ وَلَا بَنُونَ states the final boundary of wealth's usefulness that 92:11 stages as the owner's fall.
luna: The exception in the next verse is whoever comes to God with a sound heart. It completes the limit on wealth in 26:88 with an inward condition, alongside the section's purifying gift.
terra: The she-camel has a drink-share and the people have a drink-share on a known day; an animal and a precisely measured portion meet without gaming arrows.
terra: Whatever people are given is temporary worldly enjoyment, whereas مَا عِندَ اللَّهِ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَى; the “with” relation distinguishes temporary custody from lasting possession.

terra: وَرَبُّكَ يَخْلُقُ مَا يَشَاءُ وَيَخْتَارُ ... مَا كَانَ لَهُمُ الْخِيَرَةُ says creation and selection belong to the Lord and denies creatures the final choice, the clearest reversal of the deciding lot.

luna: The section cites this verse's wording that praise belongs to God in the first and the Hereafter. It applies the same temporal pair to praise and judgment, alongside the section's claim about God's ownership of both. | terra: لَهُ الْحَمْدُ فِي الْأُولَى وَالْآخِرَةِ joins divine possession of first and last to praise, and its closing judgment and return explain what that ownership entails.

luna: This verse tells Qarun to seek the Hereafter through what God has given him, while not neglecting his share of this world. It connects property to seeking the lasting good rather than treating possession as final. | terra: Seek the last abode with what God has given while not forgetting نَصِيبَكَ مِنَ الدُّنْيَا and doing good as He did good to you; the two shares are ordered through received wealth and renewed giving.

terra: Qarun says his wealth was given because of knowledge he possesses, but the ayah recalls people God destroyed who were stronger and greater in accumulation; “given” property cannot establish independent ownership.
terra: People desiring worldly life wish for Qarun's like and call him one of great fortune; حَظّ is precisely the apparent lucky share that the passage will overturn.
terra: People of knowledge answer the wishers in 28:79 that God's reward is better for believers who act rightly, moving value from Qarun's visible portion to the final one.
terra: God causes the earth to swallow Qarun and his home, and neither his party nor he can help him; possessed wealth and social power fail at the owner's literal fall.

terra: Those who had wished for Qarun's place recognize that God expands and restricts provision and could have swallowed them too; the scene ends by identifying the allocator behind the fortune they envied.
terra: Worldly life is only amusement and play, whereas the hereafter is the true life; the gaming scene becomes an emblem of a portion that cannot last.
terra: God originates creation and repeats it, and His is the highest attribute in the heavens and earth; creation and divine height meet in one claim.
terra: A parable asks whether human owners make those they possess equal partners in the provision God gave them; it uses their own property instincts to clarify exclusive divine ownership.

luna: This verse distinguishes money given for increase from alms given seeking God's face. It clarifies the section's contrast between a material stake in maysir and giving for the Lord's pleasure. | terra: A gift intended to grow فِي أَمْوَالِ النَّاسِ does not grow with God, whereas zakat تُرِيدُونَ وَجْهَ اللَّهِ does; wealth, purification, and seeking God's face reproduce 92:18–20 while excluding a human return.

luna: The section's dictionary sense for root خ ل ق includes measuring leather before cutting. This verse commands David to measure the links of his armor carefully; the craft is a specific parallel in fitting measured material, though it concerns armor rather than leather.
terra: The wealthy claim نَحْنُ أَكْثَرُ أَمْوَالًا وَأَوْلَادًا and infer they will not be punished; the scene exposes the false conversion of a large worldly share into final security.
terra: The Lord expands and restricts provision for whom He wills; answering the boast in 34:35, this identifies wealth as apportioned provision, not proof of its holder's rank.

luna: The verse says wealth and children do not bring people near to God; faith and righteous action do. It distinguishes possession from the standing the section assigns to generosity and seeking the Lord's face. | terra: وَمَا أَمْوَالُكُمْ وَلَا أَوْلَادُكُم بِالَّتِي تُقَرِّبُكُمْ عِندَنَا denies that possessions bring their owners near; faith and righteous action, not the share held, determine doubled recompense.
terra: The Lord who expands and restricts provision replaces whatever is spent and is the best provider, joining measured allotment to voluntary giving.
terra: Whoever purifies himself does so for his own benefit, and the destination is to God; it explains why the giver's purification does not create a debt in the recipient.

terra: When told to spend from what God provided, disbelievers object that God could feed the needy Himself; their refusal mistakes being entrusted with provision for freedom from the Provider's claim.
terra: God created cattle by His own making and فَهُمْ لَهَا مَالِكُونَ; the ayah grants real human ownership inside a prior divine act of creation.

luna: Jonah takes part in a draw and is among those who lose; 37:142 completes the consequence by saying the fish swallowed him. The lot here exposes someone to loss, unlike the section's winner's share. | terra: فَسَاهَمَ فَكَانَ مِنَ الْمُدْحَضِينَ stages an actual lot on the ship; unlike meysir, it allocates an emergency burden rather than distributing a slaughtered prize, marking the boundary between lot-casting and gambling.
terra: The ayah joins creation from one soul and its mate, repeated creation in wombs, رَبُّكُمْ, and لَهُ الْمُلْكُ; it gathers the source's creator, pair, Lord, and owner into one scene.
terra: The ayah asks whether people know that God expands and restricts provision for whom He wills; it is another explicit formulation of the measured worldly share.

terra: People fail to measure God according to His true measure, while the whole earth is in His grasp and the heavens folded in His hand; human measures and holdings are dwarfed by the Owner's scale.
terra: لِّمَنِ الْمُلْكُ الْيَوْمَ ... لِلَّهِ answers the final day's ownership question explicitly, when no human claim or drawn share remains.
terra: The ayah joins God's creating and forming people, providing good things, and being their Lord; the creator, provider, and owner functions gathered by the source belong to one speaker.
terra: Everything in the heavens and earth belongs to God, who is the Most High and Great; ownership and divine height meet without the gaming image's “highest” arrow.
terra: The keys of heavens and earth belong to God, who expands and restricts provision; ownership of the stores and allotment from them are joined.

luna: The verse contrasts those seeking the harvest of the Hereafter with those seeking the worldly harvest, for whom it says there is no share in the Hereafter. It makes the section's contrast between a worldly payout and an enduring allotment explicit. | terra: The seeker of the worldly harvest receives some of it yet has وَمَا لَهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ مِن نَّصِيبٍ; this restates the image's first-versus-last share in agricultural rather than gaming terms.

luna: This verse says that if God expanded provision without limit people would overreach, so He sends it down by a measure as He wills. It gives the section's measured shares a divine limit rather than a lottery's contingency.
terra: Worldly gifts are temporary enjoyment, and what is عِندَ اللَّهِ is better and more lasting for believers who trust their Lord; the ayah repeats the image's ownership boundary.
terra: لِلَّهِ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ is followed by creation at will and the gift of females or males; dominion, creating the two sexes, and allotting a gift all belong to one giver.
terra: God pairs males and females or makes whom He wills barren; continuing 42:49, this ayah makes the human “share” of offspring a knowledgeable divine allotment rather than a claim of ownership.

luna: The verse explicitly says, نَحْنُ قَسَمْنَا بَيْنَهُم مَّعِيشَتَهُمْ, “We divided their livelihood among them,” and mentions differing degrees. It locates material allotment with God rather than chance. | terra: أَهُمْ يَقْسِمُونَ رَحْمَتَ رَبِّكَ challenges human division, while نَحْنُ قَسَمْنَا بَيْنَهُم مَّعِيشَتَهُمْ assigns worldly livelihoods and ranks to the Lord.

terra: God could give disbelievers silver roofs and stairways if that would not make humanity one unbelieving community; the hypothetical shows how little a lavish worldly allotment signifies, leading to 43:35.
terra: Silver doors and couches continue the hypothetical property display of 43:33, whose status as mere worldly enjoyment is stated in 43:35.
terra: The silver and gold furnishings described in 43:33–34 are only worldly enjoyment, while the hereafter with the Lord is for the reverent; lavish possession is reduced to a temporary share.
terra: All have degrees according to what they did so that God may pay their deeds in full without wrong; final rank is an exact earned allotment rather than chance.
terra: Worldly life is play and amusement, whereas belief and reverence bring reward, and God does not ask people for all their wealth; moral ease and recompense do not arise from the world's game.
terra: If God pressed people for their wealth, they would withhold and their resentments would emerge; this directly prepares the call to spend and the exposure of stinginess in 47:38.
terra: Those called to spend include one who withholds, but فَإِنَّمَا يَبْخَلُ عَن نَّفْسِهِ and اللَّهُ الْغَنِيُّ expose stinginess as self-harm before the true, need-free owner.
terra: God created people from male and female, then made peoples and tribes, but honor with God rests on reverence; created distinctions do not allot final rank by lineage or fortune.
terra: وَفِي أَمْوَالِهِمْ حَقٌّ لِّلسَّائِلِ وَالْمَحْرُومِ likewise locates another person's due within their wealth, making ownership carry an obligation to share.

luna: The section asks who owns one's share and cites the question, “Does a human have whatever he desires?” This verse challenges desire as a claim to possession. | terra: أَمْ لِلْإِنسَانِ مَا تَمَنَّى denies that a person's wish creates a possession or allotted outcome, exposing the false premise behind relying on a lucky arrow.

luna: The answer to 53:24 is that the Hereafter and the first life belong to God (فَلِلَّهِ الْآخِرَةُ وَالْأُولَىٰ). It directly grounds the section's claim that first and last are God's. | terra: فَلِلَّهِ الْآخِرَةُ وَالْأُولَى is the exact ownership claim of 92:13 and locates both the first and last with the one who measures the share.
terra: To God belongs all in heavens and earth so that evil and good may be repaid by their deeds; ownership and just recompense replace fortune as the basis of the final share.
terra: وَأَن لَّيْسَ لِلْإِنسَانِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَى assigns a person what he strives for, replacing wished-for or randomly drawn possession with accountable effort.
terra: His striving will be seen; this continues 53:39 and makes the basis of the coming allotment manifest rather than hidden in a chance draw.
terra: ثُمَّ يُجْزَاهُ الْجَزَاءَ الْأَوْفَى promises the fullest repayment for the seen striving, giving “a favor repaid” its just divine rather than human setting.
terra: وَأَنَّ إِلَى رَبِّكَ الْمُنتَهَى closes 53:39–41 at the Lord, so the final accounting and destination return to the owner named in the source.
terra: God created the two mates, male and female, an exact repeated formulation of the created pair in 92:3.
terra: الْمَاءَ قِسْمَةٌ بَيْنَهُمْ makes water an apportioned share between the people and the she-camel announced in 54:27, a divinely set turn rather than a random prize.

luna: The section links the root خ ل ق in 92:3 to an allotted share; this verse says, إِنَّا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْنَاهُ بِقَدَرٍ, joining creation to measure. | terra: إِنَّا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْنَاهُ بِقَدَرٍ directly binds creation to measure, turning “cut to measure before division” into a claim about every created thing.

luna: The verse calls believers to spend from what God has made them successors over (مُسْتَخْلَفِينَ فِيهِ). That directly grounds the section's claim that one's مال is held under God's ownership and should be given. | terra: Spend from what God جَعَلَكُم مُّسْتَخْلَفِينَ فِيهِ: the giver can call wealth his, yet holds it as a successor, which makes divine ownership the ground of giving.

luna: This verse distinguishes the rank of those who spent and fought before victory from those who acted later, while promising good to both. It links rank to costly action rather than to the section's highest arrow winning a share. | terra: The question “why do you not spend?” is grounded in وَلِلَّهِ مِيرَاثُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ, so refusing a gift cannot prevent the owner from inheriting it.
terra: Charitable men and women who lend God a good loan have it multiplied and receive a noble reward; giving property becomes a measured final return from its true owner.
terra: Those who are stingy and command stinginess are answered that God is the self-sufficient, praiseworthy one; the holder's refusal cannot make him the true owner.

luna: Here the wealth and children of God's opponents will not avail them against Him; the verse places them among the people of the Fire. It specifies the afterlife boundary of the section's property theme. | terra: Neither wealth nor children avail against God, and their owners become companions of the fire; this connects the failed property of 92:11 to its warned fire.

luna: This verse directs distribution of communal gains to named recipients so wealth will not circulate only among the rich. It gives a social rule for sharing property, contrasting with the section's lot-drawn winner. | terra: God-directed distribution of recovered property is designed كَيْ لَا يَكُونَ دُولَةً بَيْنَ الْأَغْنِيَاءِ, so a communal share does not circulate only among wealthy possessors.
terra: They prefer others over themselves despite need, and protection from the self's stinginess marks success; this is a social distribution governed by generosity instead of chance.

luna: The verse warns believers not to let wealth and children distract them from God's remembrance. It identifies a particular way possession can obstruct the giving and devotion that distinguish the section's two paths. | terra: Believers are warned not to let wealth and children distract them from God's remembrance, since those who do so are the losers; possession can produce loss rather than ease.

luna: This verse tells people to spend from what God provided before death comes. It connects the section's held wealth and its failure at the end with an urgent opportunity to give while one still has it. | terra: Spend from what God provided before death arrives and the holder asks for delay so he might give charity; retained provision becomes unusable when apparent ownership ends.
luna: This closes the warning in 63:9–10 by saying God will not delay a soul when its appointed time comes. Its own contribution is the finality that makes spending before death consequential.

luna: This verse calls wealth and children a trial; 64:16 follows by telling people to spend from what God provided and resist stinginess. Its own contribution is to frame the section's property and giving choice as a test. | terra: Wealth and children are only a trial, and with God is a great reward; the repeated formulation separates the held share from the final one.

luna: This verse commands spending from what God has provided and calls protection from one's own stinginess success. It spells out the section's giving-versus-withholding distinction as a choice about God's provision. | terra: Hear, obey, and spend for your own good; whoever is guarded from the self's stinginess prospers, directly rendering 92's giver-and-miser division.
terra: A good loan to God is multiplied and forgiven; the property given returns by a divinely measured increase, though the loan metaphor is broader than the source's lot scene.
terra: وَمَن يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَل لَّهُ مِنْ أَمْرِهِ يُسْرًا repeats 92's precise moral relation: reverence is followed by God-given ease.

luna: The verse tells each person to spend according to the provision given to him and promises ease after hardship (يُسْرًا). It connects the section's ease root ي س ر with spending measured by one's means, rather than a chance draw. | terra: Each person spends according to capacity and only from what God has given; سَيَجْعَلُ اللَّهُ بَعْدَ عُسْرٍ يُسْرًا unites apportioned provision, giving, and promised ease.
terra: Dominion is in God's hand and He has power over everything, a compact statement of the true ownership that governs every human portion.
terra: The ayah asks who could provide if God withheld His provision; a person's held wealth depends on a continuing allotment that its holder cannot command.
terra: The garden owners agree that no poor person will enter upon them that day; the harvest is treated as an exclusive private share and withheld before it is even gathered.
terra: After the garden is destroyed they say بَلْ نَحْنُ مَحْرُومُونَ; those who planned to deprive the poor in 68:24 discover that their own expected portion was never secured.
terra: عَسَى رَبُّنَا أَن يُبْدِلَنَا خَيْرًا مِّنْهَا ends the garden scene by returning replacement property to the Lord's allotment, though it remains a hope rather than a promise.

luna: The section says the man's wealth cannot avail him when he falls; here the condemned speaker says, ما أغنى عني ماليه, “my wealth did not avail me.” The same مال root makes the failed claim of possession explicit. | terra: مَا أَغْنَى عَنِّي مَالِيَهْ is the condemned person's own recognition that “my wealth” did not avail, exposing the limit of grammatical possession.
luna: After the failed wealth claim in 69:28, this verse says the speaker's authority has perished. It extends the section's limit on مال from possessions to worldly power.
terra: وَفِي أَمْوَالِهِمْ حَقٌّ مَّعْلُومٌ says that within “their wealth” is a known, measured right, limiting the owner's claim from inside the possession itself.
terra: The known right in 70:24 belongs to the asker and deprived, identifying the recipients whose portion the apparent owner must release.
terra: وَلَا تَمْنُن تَسْتَكْثِرُ forbids giving in order to obtain more, setting a boundary around the source's gift for which no human favor is being repaid.
terra: كَلَّا بَلْ تُحِبُّونَ الْعَاجِلَةَ names love of the immediate world as the stance opposed to the source's ownership of both first and last.
terra: وَتَذَرُونَ الْآخِرَةَ completes 75:20 by showing that preference is an abandonment of the final share, not merely enjoyment of a present one.

terra: فَجَعَلَ مِنْهُ الزَّوْجَيْنِ الذَّكَرَ وَالْأُنثَى repeats the male-female pair of 92:3 in a context where prior ayat describe creating and proportioning, supporting creation as measured formation.

luna: The section's giver parts with his wealth; this verse depicts people feeding the poor, orphan, and captive despite their own love of food. It gives concrete recipients to giving rather than taking a lot-drawn share. | terra: They give food despite loving it to the needy, orphan, and captive; this supplies the costly act whose motive is stated in 76:9 and parallels giving one's wealth to purify oneself.

luna: This explains the feeding in 76:8: the givers seek God's face and want neither recompense nor thanks. It closely matches the section's claim that the giver has no favor to repay and gives only seeking his Lord's face. | terra: إِنَّمَا نُطْعِمُكُمْ لِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ and seeking neither recompense nor thanks directly unfold 92:19–20's gift made with no human favor to repay.
terra: People love the immediate world and leave behind a heavy day; the verse identifies the preference that sacrifices the final portion for the first.
terra: Pharaoh says أَنَا رَبُّكُمُ الْأَعْلَى, seizing the exact joined titles “Lord” and “highest” for himself; his claim is the human counterfeit of 92:20.
terra: God seizes the false highest lord as a lesson of الْآخِرَةِ وَالْأُولَى; continuing 79:24, both temporal realms become the scope of judgment rather than Pharaoh's ownership.
terra: مِن نُّطْفَةٍ خَلَقَهُ فَقَدَّرَهُ states human creation and apportionment together, giving the source's “measured before cutting” sense a bodily referent.
terra: The Lord created, proportioned, and balanced the human being; creation is an act of fitting and measure, not an unmeasured cut.
terra: In whatever form God willed He assembled the person, continuing 82:7's measured formation and locating the final shape in divine choice.
terra: A soul possesses nothing for another soul on that day and الْأَمْرُ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِّلَّهِ; final ownership and disposal are exclusively God's.
luna: The surah opens by condemning those who give short measure. It gives a concrete boundary for the section's share theme: portions in exchange must not be secretly reduced.
luna: This identifies the short-measure traders as people who demand their full measure from others. It adds the one-sided taking that makes their division unjust.
luna: The same traders reduce what they measure or weigh for others. It completes the image of unjust portions in 83:1–2 and contrasts with a genuinely measured share.

luna: The section connects the root ع ل و to the highest arrow, al-Muʿallā, and to the Lord named al-Aʿlā. This verse calls Him the Most High (الْأَعْلَى), grounding that elevation in the Lord rather than the arrow's rank. | terra: سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ الْأَعْلَى repeats the source's joined title رَبِّهِ الْأَعْلَى and commands that the highest name be glorified rather than treated as the best gaming arrow.

luna: The section links creation's خ ل ق root to an allotted share. This adjacent verse says God created and proportioned (خَلَقَ فَسَوَّىٰ), joining creation to ordered form. | terra: الَّذِي خَلَقَ فَسَوَّى makes creation an act of fitting and ordering; it identifies what the Lord Most High of 87:1 does and grounds the source's measured خَلَقَ.

luna: The next verse says God measured and guided (قَدَّرَ فَهَدَىٰ). It completes the creation-and-order sequence of 87:2 and echoes the section's measured share and its claim that guidance belongs to God. | terra: وَالَّذِي قَدَّرَ فَهَدَى joins apportioning to guidance in one divine act, directly explaining why 92 makes both the measured share and guidance God's rather than the lot's.
terra: وَنُيَسِّرُكَ لِلْيُسْرَى is a divine promise of being eased toward ease; beside 87:1–3 it makes yusr the Creator's guided provision, not the result of a gaming draw.
terra: Prosperity belongs to the one who purifies himself, an exact parallel to the giver who offers wealth in order to purify himself.
terra: بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا diagnoses preference for the nearer life, the choice that turns a present share into loss of the last.
terra: وَالْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَى answers 87:16 and gives the lasting reason not to mistake the nearer allotment for the greater possession.

luna: The verse depicts a man treating expanded provision as proof that his Lord honored him. It parallels the section's property-and-rank image, then its context challenges that reading. | terra: A person whose Lord honors and favors him says “my Lord has honored me”; the ayah stages human interpretation of a divinely given share.

luna: The man in this verse treats restricted provision as humiliation; the wording says God measured his provision (قَدَرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقَهُ). It makes an allotted share concrete, while the next ayah rejects the man's interpretation. | terra: When the Lord measures his provision, the person says he has been humiliated; قَدَرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقَهُ exposes the mistake of treating a smaller allotment as a verdict on worth.

luna: The “No!” here corrects the claim in 89:15–16: the problem is failure to honor the orphan. It supports the section's account of moral difference as giving, not the amount of wealth received. | terra: كَلَّا answers both readings in 89:15–16 and points instead to failure to honor the orphan, shifting worth from what one receives to how one gives.

luna: The same correction says people do not urge one another to feed the poor. It supplies a specific failure to give, echoing the section's distinction between generosity and withholding. | terra: Failure to urge feeding the poor continues the correction of 89:15–17: moral rank lies in sharing provision, not in the amount allotted.

luna: The verse describes devouring inheritance wholesale. It connects the section's property and apportioned shares to what happens when people consume others' portions instead of giving. | terra: After the correction about measured provision and failure to feed the poor, people consume inheritance voraciously; inherited property becomes an unjustly swallowed share.

luna: The verse condemns excessive love of wealth. It names the inward attachment that stands against the section's giver, who parts with property for God's face. | terra: The passage closes by naming an excessive love of wealth, explaining the possessive instinct behind the misreading and withholding in 89:15–19.

luna: The section describes giving wealth to purify oneself; this verse says the one who purifies the soul succeeds. It supplies a direct Quranic statement of the purification the section associates with giving. | terra: Success belongs to the one who purifies the soul; this states the result of the self-purification sought through giving in 92:18.

luna: The next verse gives the reverse of 91:9: the one who corrupts the soul fails. It sharpens the section's contrast between giving that purifies and withholding. | terra: Failure belongs to the one who corrupts or buries the soul, completing 91:9 with the opposite outcome to purification.
terra: نَاقَةَ اللَّهِ وَسُقْيَاهَا names both God's she-camel and her allotted drink, placing ownership and share under God's sign before the people destroy it.

luna: The verse says the Hereafter will be better for the Prophet than the first life. It repeats the section's first/last pair while adding a particular promise of the latter's superiority. | terra: وَلَلْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ لَّكَ مِنَ الْأُولَى gives the first and last a value-order for the Prophet, while 92:13 states whose they are.
terra: رَبِّكَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ directly joins the Lord to creating, the same link the source draws between 92:20 and 92:3.
terra: أَن رَّآهُ اسْتَغْنَى gives self-sufficiency as the reason the human transgresses, exposing the stance of the miser who treats wealth as enough.
terra: إِنَّ إِلَى رَبِّكَ الرُّجْعَى answers the imagined self-sufficiency of 96:7 with return to the Lord, where human possession ends.
luna: The verse says whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it. It makes the section's ease-by-giving claim a measured moral outcome rather than a chance payout.
luna: The paired verse says whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it. It completes the measured return of 99:7 and sets a moral boundary around the section's distribution-by-chance scene.
luna: The verse describes those whose scales are heavy, making deeds the measure of outcome. It contrasts the section's arrow-drawn share with a weighed judgment.
luna: The person with heavy scales is promised a pleasant life. This gives the measured outcome in 101:6 its result, echoing the section's ease for the giver.
luna: The verse turns to the person whose scales are light. It makes the section's contrary outcome for withholding a matter of measured deeds rather than a chance draw.
luna: This names the light-weighed person's destination as the abyss, completing 101:8. It gives the consequence of the opposite measured outcome, a boundary to the section's ease.
terra: The one who جَمَعَ مَالًا وَعَدَّدَهُ treats wealth as something accumulated and counted, the possessive attitude tested by 92:11.
terra: يَحْسَبُ أَنَّ مَالَهُ أَخْلَدَهُ states the hoarder's false conclusion; wealth cannot confer permanence and instead fails exactly where the final owner matters.

luna: The section says مال will not avail its owner; this verse says Abu Lahab's wealth and earnings did not avail him (ما أغنى عنه ماله وما كسب). It gives another explicit reversal of wealth's presumed power. | terra: مَا أَغْنَى عَنْهُ مَالُهُ وَمَا كَسَبَ is an almost verbal twin of 92:11: acquired wealth gives no protection at the decisive fall.
